recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: employee + audit
recommended_phases.rationale: Leaf modules with zero internal dependencies. Employee provides identity/manager lookup; audit provides the write-only audit trail required by GP-002. Both are needed by every other module.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Policy engine
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on employee (Phase 1). Encodes leave-type rules, max-days, and request validation. balance and leave both need it.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Balance tracking
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on policy (Phase 2) and audit (Phase 1). Manages per-employee/per-type/per-year balances with deduct/credit/initialize. leave depends on it.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Notification
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on employee (Phase 1). Can be built in parallel with Phases 2–3. leave depends on it.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Leave orchestration
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all four prior phases. Orchestrates apply/approve/reject/cancel with policy validation, balance deduction, audit recording, and notification dispatch.

app_notes: Layer boundaries follow the existing pattern (model → repository → service → controller → routes). Dependencies flow inward: leave (orchestrator) depends on balance, policy, employee, audit, and notification. balance depends on policy and audit. policy depends on employee. notification depends on employee. audit and employee are leaf modules with no internal dependencies. No circular edges exist. Every service method is defined via an interface before implementation. GP-002 (audit) is satisfied by the audit module recording all state changes. GP-005 (RBAC) is enforced at the controller/route layer — not designed here but noted as a requirement for the design agent. The dual naming convention in ARCHITECTURE.md (dot-notation files vs PascalCase directories) is resolved by standardizing on the dot-notation pattern already used by the existing status and uptime modules.
